A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QualiSpeech study. Their main text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–J support comparison, including matching material across figure consolidation and pagination changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original auditory-LLM benchmark and finetuning results, plus encoder ablations, generalization experiments, and annotation-consistency analyses in Appendix J.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–13 and the accompanying main-text and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The annotation pipeline and SALMONN-7B adaptation remain unchanged, including GPT-generated descriptions, human revision, Q-former/LoRA finetuning, and subsequent training on descriptive comments.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same English synthetic, real, and simulated-real speech sources and evaluate the same seven scored and four descriptive aspects. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains SALMONN-7B, SALMONN-13B, Qwen-Audio-Chat, Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct, and WavLLM. Table 4 retains Vicuna-v1.5-7B and GPT-4o-mini; comparison membership elsewhere is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, ten-epoch training, balancing and joint-training settings, evaluation metrics, and multiple-annotation evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The revised PCC wording in Section 4.2.1 aligns with the metric already specified in v1.

E4.justification: Both retain the training-strategy and description-format comparisons, encoder ablations, cross-domain generalization tests, holistic-description scoring, and multiple-annotation analyses. Appendix J is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix J.4 retains the same inter-annotator correlations and annotation-aggregation procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–13 retain their numerical entries. Section 4.2.1 replaces the speed-highest-accuracy and noise-accuracy-over-60% account with noise PCC around 0.7. The redrawn distribution chart also changes displayed frequencies: overall-quality rating 3 rises from approximately 3,800 in v1 Figure 11 to 4,400 in v3 Figure 5, without an accompanying explanation.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. The existing metric descriptions and annotation-aggregation definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: QualiSpeech's detailed annotations, its benchmark, descriptive speech-quality assessment with auditory LLMs, and the potential value of reasoning.

C2.justification: V3 removes the interpretation that naturalness and overall quality are the hardest aspects to predict because they depend on more subjective judgments. The other mechanism explanations, generalization interpretations, and stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract changes dataset access from a promised future release to reported availability at the same Hugging Face location. Implementation details, prompts, annotation information, and licensing remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are unchanged, including the claimed dataset novelty and Appendix A's treatment of natural-language assessment and MOS as complementary.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized prose and cross-reference edits, adds Lu Lu to the author list, identifies the corresponding author, and adds funding acknowledgments. The main narrative and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V1's seven separate distribution plots, Figures 5–11, become one grouped, color-coded chart with a shared count axis and rating legend in v3 Figure 5. Subsequent figures are renumbered and appendix content reflows; the main figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves consistency between Section 4.2.1 and Table 2 and reports dataset availability. However, its redesigned distribution chart changes some frequencies without explaining whether these correct earlier statistics or reflect changed data. The PDFs do not resolve the accuracy of this change to the dataset evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality effect.
